name: @sjawhar/claude-envoy
description: Claude Code plugin for Legion's Envoy bus
//: test: each command's --timeout is at least twice the slowest row or hook it ran under 8 busy loops on 2 CPUs at 61b66deb (two runs in a builds Job).

The first, 17000: read again at the round-3 class-search tree (main 46c275dcba with #4437's head e9d8f5075f and its uncommitted fixes), the whole command under the same load (two runs in builds Job d2-c9-ce, 2026-11-19): the fresh bundles contain only runtime builtin module specifiers, 7,115.80 and 8,211.25 ms, which the 15000 it had before held only 1.83 times; Bun prints no hook times, so no hook is read there. Before that, at 15000: a Legion pane's server registers on its transcript, claims its role, serves the legion tool and delivers through the inbox, 5,687.14 ms (the slowest hook, packed-skills.test.ts's beforeAll, 984.92 ms). The codex files main's #4406 added read later, under the same 8 loops: their slowest row, codex-owner.test.ts's two server processes racing for a dead owner's place, took 4,803.83 and 5,078.79 ms at d22477d9 (two runs in builds Job d5-8, 2026-11-19; 2,970.21 and 3,190.70 ms in d4-codex-8-3 at fdce4e94d2), under the 7,500 ms half of this guard. Read again at 6ca1a534 with #4437's fourth merge, the whole command under the same load with the files main's #4140 gave row timeouts of their own (two runs each in builds Jobs d8-ce-first-8 and d8-ce-first-8b): the slowest row, the fresh bundles contain only runtime builtin module specifiers, took 7,291.90 ms (6,991.86 ms in d8-ce-first-8b, once the 401 row held its two credential shares rather than waiting them out, 8,284.27 ms before). The five files of main's #4353 whose rows run a whole channel-server process (codex-reopen, envoy-channel-live-view-clear, envoy-channel-mcp, envoy-channel-reopen and envoy-channel-start-reopen) lost their 600,000 ms rows and 120,000 ms waits (main read one such row at 25.8 s alone) and ran in the second command until their reading at #4655's head d75ea661f5, the five files alone under the same load (three runs in builds Job ce-r-five-8, 2026-11-20), which puts them here: their slowest row, envoy-channel-reopen.test.ts's connection closed for good under the session's broker token, reopened presenting a token, took 5,601.12 ms (5,317.25 and 5,395.89 ms in the other two runs); they have no hooks. Read again with them in it, the whole command under the same load at d75ea661f5 with this test script (three runs in builds Job ce-r-first-8, 2026-11-20, 594 rows passing in each): the slowest row, the fresh bundles contain only runtime builtin module specifiers, took 6,805.14 ms, and that envoy-channel-reopen.test.ts row 6,297.64 ms. CI's 10,829.06 ms for envoy-channel-start-reopen.test.ts's Codex stop row at 06d1a05bab (run 44834565221) was no correct run: the row left the hub's PINGs unanswered after the start's flush, so a dial the hub admitted before the row held the next one waited out its 10 s dial bound before the stop (about 590 ms and one such bound; reproduced 4 of 4 with a record of the server's dial timers, and never in 90 unforced rows beside 8 busy loops, builds Job legion-load-run-fxppr). With the row fixed, the start-reopen, role-reassertion and channel-fatal-exit files alone under the same load (three runs in builds Job legion-load-run-2dm5g, 2026-11-21) took at most 2,781.22 ms a start-reopen row and 4,721.81 ms a channel-fatal-exit row.

The second, 120000: a turn that ends with a background task running earns no reminder, 19,096.00 ms here; envoy-channel-stall.test.ts runs only with LEGION_E2E_ENVOY_STACK=1, and there its rows took up to 53,001.47 ms (its beforeAll 14,816.41 ms) under the same load. channel-nats.test.ts (main's #4140) runs here too: its start that waits through a broker refusing connections took 12,293.66 ms in d8-ce-moved-8, above the first's half, and 14,600.88 ms in ce-r-second-8 (below). Main's codex-connection-proof.test.ts and codex-prints-no-secret.test.ts (#4490) and packed-skills.test.ts's two long-listing rows (#3675) carried 60,000 ms rows and 20,000 ms hooks of their own, which went: the three files run here, under this guard. Read under the same load at d75ea661f5 with this test script (three runs in builds Job ce-r-second-8, 2026-11-20), their slowest rows took 1,804.72 ms (codex-connection-proof), 1,700.42 ms (codex-prints-no-secret) and 6,186.68 ms (packed-skills, the release's check of a listing longer than a pipe holds); Bun prints no hook times, so their hooks, which carried 20,000 ms on main, have no reading, and the three stay here.

The third, 300000, runs codex-real.test.ts alone, which runs only where LEGION_TEST_CODEX names a Codex binary, and no CI job or builds Job has one: it is the 300,000 ms its beforeAll carried on main (#4406), not a reading.

scripts.test: bun test --timeout=17000 --preload @legion/test-fixtures/row-deadline --path-ignore-patterns='tests/{answers-claude,build-inputs,build-out,channel-nats,codex-connection-proof,codex-prints-no-secret,codex-real,envoy-channel-stall,legion-phase-hook-claude,packed-skills}.test.ts' && bun test --timeout=120000 --preload @legion/test-fixtures/row-deadline ./tests/answers-claude.test.ts ./tests/build-inputs.test.ts ./tests/build-out.test.ts ./tests/envoy-channel-stall.test.ts ./tests/legion-phase-hook-claude.test.ts ./tests/channel-nats.test.ts ./tests/codex-connection-proof.test.ts ./tests/codex-prints-no-secret.test.ts ./tests/packed-skills.test.ts && bun test --timeout=300000 --preload @legion/test-fixtures/row-deadline ./tests/codex-real.test.ts
